meta.title: Cosmetics & Personal Care Tooling - Closures, Jars, Dispenser Components | Metal Form
meta.description: Mould design and manufacture for cosmetic closures, jars, pump and mechanism components. Multi-cavity tooling to 46 cavities, hot and cold runner, threaded cores, cosmetic surface finish. Engineering, DFM, reverse engineering and ongoing supply. Persian engineering since 2006.

name: Cosmetics & Personal Care
tile: Show-surface tooling. Polish grade, parting line and gate decided before the steel is cut.

headline: The mould
is the finish.
hero.lead: Closures, jars, dispenser and mechanism components. The show surface is not applied after moulding — it is copied off the steel, one unit at a time. Send the part or the model. We assess the geometry, the tooling route and the production economics.

surface.heading: Moulding does not add a finish. It copies one.
surface.body: Polish grade, texture, parting line, gate position and draft are cut into steel once. Every unit after that carries them. This is why a cosmetic tool is bought differently from a functional one, and why the decisions that matter most are the cheapest ones on the programme.
surface.railAttribution: Grades, roughness values, neck codes and cost ratios on this page are published industry practice. They are not Metal Form measurements.
surface.railNda: An NDA can be signed before detailed technical disclosure. Before a launch, the geometry is the commercial secret.

callouts.note: A witness line where the two halves of the mould meet, reproduced on every part. On a show face its position is a design decision, not a manufacturing detail.
The mark where the part left the feed. It can be flattened, reduced and moved. It cannot be removed, so it is placed.
Specified per face, not per part. A mirror where the consumer looks, matte or textured where nobody does.
The flat annular face that actually seals. Hidden, unforgiving, and unrelated to how the pack looks.
Set by the texture depth that was specified, not by convention. Too little draft and the part drags and scuffs on ejection.

surface.close: None of these five are adjustable once the steel is cut.

gloss.heading: Gloss is hand labour. You buy it one face at a time.
gloss.body: SPI grades are a polish scale reached with diamond compound and a polisher's hands. VDI 3400 is a separate roughness scale burned in by EDM. They are not interchangeable and they correlate only approximately. The difference between them is where most cosmetic tooling money is either spent well or wasted.
gloss.note: On the VDI scale every six units roughly doubles roughness. Texture depth then sets the minimum draft, and the part that was drawn without enough of it comes off the core scuffed.

specLabels.steel: What it asks of the steel

rungs.name: SPI A-1
rungs.cost: The most bench time on this ladder, and bench time is a person rather than a machine. It buys lead time as well as cost.
rungs.steel: A clean, inclusion-free block, through-hardened. A mirror shows every defect in the steel and every fingerprint of the polishing.
rungs.draft: Governed by geometry and ejection, not by the finish.

rungs.name: SPI A-2
rungs.cost: Materially less bench time than A-1 for a difference most packs do not carry. The common premium cosmetic show surface.
rungs.steel: Still wants a fine-grained hardened steel. Weld repairs on a polished face are visible.
rungs.draft: Governed by geometry and ejection, not by the finish.

rungs.name: SPI A-3
rungs.cost: Gloss without the mirror. The sensible grade for a face the consumer sees at arm's length rather than in a hand.
rungs.steel: Standard hardened tool steel is adequate.
rungs.draft: Governed by geometry and ejection, not by the finish.

rungs.name: SPI B-1
rungs.cost: Paper rather than diamond. A semi-gloss that reads as finished but does not hold a reflection.
rungs.draft: Governed by geometry and ejection, not by the finish.

rungs.name: SPI C-1
rungs.cost: A satin working surface. Correct for the inside of a closure, a liner or a face that will be over-decorated.
rungs.draft: Governed by geometry and ejection, not by the finish.

rungs.name: VDI 24
rungs.cost: Cut electrically rather than polished by hand, so cost tracks the texturing operation rather than the polisher.
rungs.steel: Texture depth is burned into the surface, so a repair to a textured face means re-texturing it.

rungs.name: VDI 36
rungs.cost: A deep, obviously tactile grain. Hides sink and flow marks that a gloss face would publish.
rungs.steel: Deep texture removes material. It has to be allowed for in the cavity dimension, not discovered afterwards.

rungs.name: VDI 42
rungs.cost: Coarse. Almost never a cosmetic show surface, frequently the right answer on a grip or a base.
rungs.steel: Same constraint as VDI 36, further along.
rungs.draft: More again than VDI 36 asks for, or the part scuffs on the way out.

gloss.close: Specify the grade per face rather than per part. A mirror on the one face the consumer studies and a texture everywhere else means the tool costs what the pack actually needs, not what the drawing note happened to say.
gloss.downstream: A polished or textured moulded face is also the substrate a decorator has to work on. Hot stamping wants clean bold geometry, metallisation wants a defect-free surface, screen printing wants a stable datum. Those processes are run downstream by specialist decorators. We design the part to suit the one you choose.

gate.heading: The gate is placed. It is never removed.
gate.body: Every moulded part carries a mark where it left the feed and a witness line where the mould halves met. Both are permanent. The only decision available is where they sit, and that decision belongs with whoever owns the artwork, taken before steel rather than at sampling.

cases.name: Direct gate, on the crown
cases.consequence: The shortest flow path and the simplest tool. It also puts a vestige standing proud exactly where the eye lands and where the decorator has to print. Correct only when the crown is hidden under an overcap.

cases.name: Sub-gate, inside the skirt
cases.consequence: The part degates itself on ejection and the vestige sits inside the skirt where nothing sees it. It costs a short cold runner and a little cycle time, and it is the default answer on most cosmetic closures.

cases.name: Valve gate, top face
cases.consequence: A pin closes the gate mechanically, giving a flat repeatable vestige and independent control of every drop in the layout. It buys a hot half, a controller and a maintenance package with it.

gate.partingHeading: The same closure, three parting lines
gate.partingBody: Where the mould splits is a second permanent mark, and it is the one the travelling highlight finds first. A parting line placed on an edge the geometry already has costs nothing to hide.

partingCases.name: On the crown radius
partingCases.note: The shortest tooling route. It also drops the split precisely where the specular band breaks, so the eye is led straight to it.

partingCases.name: At the shoulder step
partingCases.note: The line disappears into an edge the design already carries. On most closures and overcaps this is the right answer.

partingCases.name: Below the knurl
partingCases.note: Invisible on the pack, but it drives the split deep into the skirt and asks more of the steel fit and the clamp than the other two.

gate.close: Agreed before steel, this is a conversation. Discovered at sampling, it is a new cavity insert and a launch date that has already been announced.

atlas.heading: Not one part family. Eight separate tooling briefs.
atlas.body: A screw cap, a double-wall jar and a mascara wiper have almost nothing in common except the person buying them. The show surface decides everything on three of these and is irrelevant on the rest.

rows.name: Continuous-thread screw cap
rows.note: A standard solution for threaded closures. The thread provides retention and the land provides the seal. The release method for the internal thread — unscrewing drive, stripper ring or collapsible core — determines cycle time, tool cost and required spares.

rows.name: Flip-top and hinged closure
rows.note: Flow has to cross the hinge correctly and the hinge is flexed while still warm to orient the polymer. Gate position decides whether it survives years of use or whitens and cracks in month four.

rows.name: Disc-top and press-top cap
rows.note: A sprung disc pivoting inside a dome, held in a narrow tolerance band across an assembly. Stress whitening at the undercut is the failure that shows up long after approval.

rows.name: Thick-wall and double-wall jar
rows.spec: One heavy moulding, or two assembled
rows.note: Thick wall chases a glass-like flush surface and pays for it in resin and cooling time. Double wall buys the same look with less material and lets a small fill occupy a larger pack. On both, sink control is the entire job.

rows.name: Pump and dispenser components
rows.note: Function is dimensional, not visual. Cavity-to-cavity variation does not appear as a cosmetic defect here — it appears as dose variation, which is worse, because nobody sees it at inspection.

rows.name: Airless chassis and piston follower
rows.note: The follower rides up the inside wall as the pack empties. Bore ovality and follower diameter have to be controlled as one dimension rather than two, or the pack stops dosing before it is empty.

rows.name: Mascara wiper and moulded applicator
rows.note: The wiper meters product on withdrawal; the moulded applicator carries arches, hooks and petal forms a fraction of a millimetre across. Nothing in this format is about gloss. It is about small features holding their shape.

rows.name: Compact and palette body
rows.note: The hardest cosmetic surface in the sector. Sink over a boss, a flow line off the gate and any variation in gloss all read across a flat lid, and none of them can be corrected after moulding.

atlas.close: Send the part. The tooling route is decided by the geometry in front of us, not by the category it is sold in.

seal.heading: The thread retains the closure. The land does the sealing.
seal.body: A cosmetic component almost never ships alone. It meets a neck somebody else moulded, a pump somebody else assembled and a filling line somebody else set up. That interface is a published code, and the code is where packs fail.
seal.codeBody: GPI and GCMI coding reads as NN-TTT. The first number is the outside diameter of the neck in millimetres. The three digits after it define the thread style: pitch, thread depth, number of turns and where the thread starts.
seal.codesNote: These cover most personal-care formats. 24-410 is the most common plastic cosmetic finish.
seal.trapHeading: 24-400 will thread onto 24-410. It will not seal.
seal.trapBody: Same diameter, different thread style. The cap stops short, cross-threads or spins free, and every dimension on both parts is correct. It happens whenever cap and bottle come from two suppliers and nobody read the second three digits.
seal.torqueHeading: Torque is a window, not an opinion
seal.torqueBody: Application and removal torque are specified as a range and verified through a production run under ASTM D2063. Under-torque leaks in transit. Over-torque damages the pack and generates complaints. Whether a liner, a wad or a moulded sealing bead does the work is a design decision taken before the tool exists, not a correction applied to it afterwards.
seal.failuresHeading: Five ways a correct-looking part fails

failures.note: Passes visual inspection. Leaks on a pallet, in a truck, in an aircraft hold.

failures.term: A weld line behind a core
failures.note: Two flow fronts rejoined and the seam is weaker than the wall around it. That is where a cap splits under application torque.
The core cooled unevenly, or the parts were stacked warm. It gauges round at the press and not the next morning.

failures.term: A follower that will not track
failures.note: Bore ovality and follower diameter drifted apart across the cavities. The airless pack stops dosing before it is empty.
Clear SAN or acrylic against fragrance oil, alcohol or an aggressive active. Every dimension was in tolerance.

seal.close: Torque measurement, leak testing and transit qualification belong to the filler and the test house. We design the geometry that has to pass them, and we say which of those a tooling change can fix.

cavities.heading: A sixteen-cavity tool costs about five times a single. It does not run sixteen times faster.
cavities.body: Cosmetic components are priced in fractions of a cent and sold in millions, so the mould is a capital decision taken against a volume forecast rather than a project expense. Two published facts govern that decision, and they pull against each other.

facts.note: Published industry practice puts a 16-cavity tool at roughly five times the cost of a single-cavity tool, not sixteen times. That is the argument for going wide.

facts.term: Output does not scale linearly either
facts.note: Cooling is roughly 80 per cent of the cycle, and a larger tool cycles slower per shot. Sixteen cavities buy something closer to three to three and a half times the output of four, not four times.
Incremental tooling cost divided by the saving per part gives the volume at which the larger tool pays for itself. Below that volume it does not, however good the forecast looked.

chart.note: Curve shapes drawn from published industry practice. Nothing on this plot is a Metal Form quotation, and the break-even on your programme is a function of your volume, your resin and your part.

cavities.riskBody: High cavitation concentrates risk. One frozen hot tip or one damaged cavity insert takes the whole tool off the press, and published industry practice reports that roughly four in five high-cavitation moulds never run at their rated capacity because fill balance was never achieved. Two medium tools sometimes beat one large one: a failure then costs capacity rather than production.
cavities.oursBody: Metal Form has built tooling up to 46 cavities. That is the band a cosmetic closure programme actually occupies — high enough to move part cost, small enough that a tool can still be balanced, maintained and reasoned about rather than merely operated.
cavities.bridgeBody: For a format that has not proved itself yet, the sensible route is a low-cavitation bridge tool sized for a market test, and a production tool sized afterwards against the volume that actually arrived. Cavitation bought against a forecast that did not turn up is the most expensive mistake in this sector.

boundary.heading: We cut the steel. The pack is finished by other people.
boundary.body: This sector runs on a chain of specialists, and a supplier who blurs the handovers costs you the schedule rather than saving it. Here is the line, stated before a quotation rather than after one.

boundary.customerHeading: What stays with you and your specialists

customer.note: Hot stamping, vacuum metallisation, electroplating, spray and soft-touch coating, in-mould labelling and screen printing are downstream processes run by specialist decorators. We design a moulded part that is compatible with the one you choose. We perform none of them.
Masterbatch matching, let-down ratio, spectrophotometry and delta E measurement sit with your compounder and your moulder. We hold no colour laboratory.
Torque and removal-force measurement to ASTM D2063, leak and vacuum testing, drop and transit qualification and AQL lot inspection are yours or your test house's.
Whether your active crazes a clear SAN or acrylic shell is answered by your chemist. We will tell you which material families the industry treats as at risk, and design around the answer you give us.
Cosmetic product compliance, recycled-content declarations and recyclability claims belong to the brand, not to the toolmaker.
Filling, capping, secondary packaging and the line equipment that does them.

boundary.close: Naming this at the start is how the handovers get scheduled, and it is most of the difference between a launch date that holds and one that quietly moves.

continuity.heading: One tool. One site. One country.
body: Most cosmetic components run on a single tool, in a single plant, in a single country. That is efficient, and it works right up until a hot tip blocks, a cavity is damaged, a supplier relationship ends or a border closes.

A duplicate tool, built to the same geometry and held somewhere else, converts a production stoppage into a schedule change. Where drawings were never handed over, the part itself is enough to work from.
The geometry stays under NDA. Build the backup first and decide later — it does not require ending anything, and it does not require telling anybody.
continuity.readiness: This is readiness, not reserved capacity. Reserving capacity is a separate contract.

The neck finish code, or the component the part has to mate with
Annual volume per SKU, and how many colour variants the tool has to serve

items.title: Surface specification, face by face
bullets: SPI A-1: 6000-grit diamond polish, roughly Ra 0.012 – 0.025 µm. The mirror grade, and the most expensive because it is hand labour.
SPI A-2: 3000-grit diamond, roughly Ra 0.025 – 0.05 µm. The common premium cosmetic show surface.
SPI A-3: 1200-grit diamond, roughly Ra 0.05 – 0.10 µm. Gloss without the mirror.
B grades are reached with paper, C grades with stone, D grades by dry blast. Acrylic takes an A-grade polish best of the common cosmetic materials.
VDI 3400 is a separate EDM roughness scale, twelve reference grades from VDI 12 (Ra 0.40 µm) to VDI 45 (Ra 18.00 µm), where every six units roughly doubles roughness.
Texture sets the minimum draft: about 1.5 – 2.0 degrees at VDI 24, 4.0 degrees or more at VDI 36. Below that the part drags and scuffs on ejection.
items.source: Figures in this panel are published industry practice, not Metal Form measurements.

items.title: Threaded and undercut cores
bullets: Unscrewing: a gear train or rack rotates the core out of the thread. Well proven, and it adds cycle time and a wear package.
Stripping ring: forces a shallow, rounded thread over the core. The fastest route, and only available to thread forms designed to strip.
Collapsible core: contracts inward for rapid release, at higher build cost and higher wear.
Slides, lifters and cams handle side undercuts, snap features and external detail.
Every mechanism is also a spares list. Cores, cavities, rings and gears should be specified and supplied with the tool rather than ordered after the first failure.
Cooling has to be routed through the mechanism rather than around it, or the cycle gained by faster demoulding is given back to a hot core.

items.title: Materials that behave differently
bullets: PP: closures, living hinges and jar liners. The hinge has to be flowed across correctly and flexed while still warm to orient the polymer.
PET: clear jars and bottles, including preform-based routes. Hygroscopic, so it must be dried or it splays.
SAN and PMMA: clear thick-wall shells and overcaps. Both need drying, and both can craze or stress-crack in contact with fragrance oils, alcohol and some actives.
ABS: the usual substrate where a part will be metallised or plated downstream by a decorator.
Acetal: stick and pump mechanisms, for low friction and dimensional stability — and a material that keeps shrinking for days after ejection.
TPE: gaskets and wipers, supplied as separate mouldings for assembly.
PCR grades: now a regulatory requirement in several markets, and less stable lot to lot in both colour and flow. The process window has to be rebuilt for them, not inherited.
items.source: Material behaviour described here is published industry practice. Compatibility with your formulation is answered by your chemist, not by us.
